blockingFindings: The outputOverflow close path calls ensureTerminated but skips process-group confirmation, so POSIX descendants may remain alive after the root child closes while a failed terminal is emitted.

The processFailure/child-stream-error close path discards pending cancellation and does not await tree termination or descendant-group confirmation; Windows and POSIX child trees can therefore outlive the failed review.
missingNegativeTests: Add overflow tests proving descendant-group confirmation occurs before failed completion and persistence remains absent.
Add stdin/stdout/stderr failure tests proving pending tree cancellation is awaited and descendant processes cannot survive terminal failure.

architectureAssessment.deepModules: Policy, context binding, trace validation, cancellation, and publication are separated into focused helpers, but failure cleanup is not consistently centralized.
architectureAssessment.hexagonalArchitecture: Child-process, filesystem, Git, and packet-authority boundaries are explicit and remain within the approved launcher scope.
architectureAssessment.eventedBoundaries: Progress and terminal events are structured and redacted, but overflow and stream-error paths do not guarantee complete cancellation event sequencing.

exactNextAction: Route output-overflow and child-stream-failure cleanup through the shared cancellation completion path, require bounded process-tree confirmation before terminal failure, add the listed negatives, and rerun all packet-required checks.
